title: Miracle on 42nd Street (2017)
description: Manhattan Plaza in Hell's Kitchen — 3,500+ residents, 70% performing artists, housed in subsidized housing that transformed a neighborhood and launched careers. A powerful case for artist housing as civic infrastructure.

title: Warfield Commons — SF's New Arts & Media Hub
description: CAST and KALW acquired the 9-floor Warfield Building at 988 Market St. for $7.3M — a permanent, below-market home for artists, journalists, and cultural workers in Mid-Market. A live, local proof of concept that creative infrastructure can be essential infrastructure.

title: Cooperation Jackson, Mississippi
description: Worker cooperatives, a community land trust, and a cultural center — built on the cooperative economics of the Black freedom movement. Now entering its second decade, and one of the most-cited models nationally for what a solidarity economy looks like in practice.

title: Red Poppy Art House, San Francisco
description: A 650-square-foot Mission District storefront that's been a community-governed, artist-run cultural space since 2003 — hosting 150+ performances, exhibitions, and workshops annually. Proof that you don't need scale to build something essential.

title: The Laundromat Project, NYC
description: A Black-rooted, POC-led nonprofit embedding artists in everyday neighborhood spaces — laundromats, bodegas, parks, gardens — to build social cohesion and civic imagination. Two decades of proof that art as everyday infrastructure works.

title: A Brief History of Black Cooperatives in the United States
description: Essential historical grounding — from Reconstruction-era mutual aid societies through today's solidarity economy movement. The lineage this work stands in.

title: The Cooperative Movement: A Brief History
description: From the Rochdale Principles (1844) to Mondragon to today's platform cooperatives — the sweep of cooperative economic history, spanning nearly two centuries and every continent.

title: The Black Arts Movement — Larry Neal
description: The foundational text of the Black Arts Movement — the aesthetic and spiritual arm of Black Power. Neal argues the artist's primary obligation is to the community, not the marketplace. Written to consolidate dignity and coherence among people under siege.

title: Emory Douglas: The Black Panther Artist (PBS)
description: Minister of Culture for the Black Panther Party and the visual architect of the BPP newspaper — at its peak the highest-circulation paper in the country. He speaks plainly about art as service, not mystified genius.

title: Arts, Culture & Creative Industries = 7.5% of California's Economy
description: Arts, culture, media, and innovation contribute $288 billion and employ 820,000+ people statewide. The single most powerful data point for making the case to any policymaker or funder.

title: Arts & Cultural Production Satellite Account (BEA / NEA)
description: Annual, state-by-state data on arts and cultural GDP contribution, employment, and compensation. California consistently ranks among the top four states nationally.
link_label: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis · bea.gov

title: The Science of Awe (Greater Good Science Center)
description: Research on awe: how experiences of vastness reduce self-focus, increase prosocial behavior, and strengthen community bonds. The intellectual grounding for why art in public life matters.

title: Why Awe Is Such an Important Emotion — Dacher Keltner
description: Foundational work on awe as a civic emotion — how it makes us more cooperative, generous, and connected.

title: The Case for Public Art (NEA Research Brief)
description: Data on how public art builds civic attachment, reduces isolation, and improves neighborhood wellbeing across income and race lines.
link_label: National Endowment for the Arts · arts.gov

title: Artwork: A Guide for Artists Building the Solidarity Economy
description: Art.coop's foundational guide — how to build collective structures, price your work, and build power without sacrificing artistic freedom. Essential reading for any culture circle.

title: What Is the Solidarity Economy?
description: Clear, accessible explainer covering principles, history, and practices. The best single-page intro for someone coming to this fresh.

title: Economics for Emancipation
description: Framework readings for understanding the solidarity economy — what it is, how it works, how to build it where you are. Good for study groups and culture circle sessions.

title: Solidarity Economy Funding Library
description: A curated directory of funders, grants, and fellowships aligned with solidarity economy work. Start looking for money that won't compromise your values.

title: Will the Revolution Be Funded?
description: The canonical text on the relationship between liberation movements and institutional funding. Foundation money has a gravitational pull that can redirect organizations away from their most radical work. Not a reason not to seek funding — a reason to seek it with your eyes open.

title: Solidarity Not Charity: Arts & Culture Grantmaking in the Solidarity Economy
description: How arts and culture funding can align with solidarity economy principles — moving from extractive philanthropy toward reciprocal, community-driven investment.

title: Money Journey Sessions — Money Health Collective
description: Free, virtual group sessions where participants share money experiences, learn together, and build real financial skills in a non-judgmental community. Facilitated by Lin Shi. Check the site for the next cohort.

title: Rocket Money (Budget Tracker)
description: Free app that syncs with bank accounts and makes your actual spending visible. Excellent starting point for artists with irregular income.

title: Managing Money as a Freelance Artist
description: Practical, judgment-free guide to budgeting on irregular income: separating accounts, saving for taxes, building an emergency fund, pricing your work.

title: The Freelancer's Guide to Taxes
description: Step-by-step guide to self-employment taxes, quarterly payments, and deductions for creative workers. Free and printable.

title: Money Stories: Understanding Your Financial Autobiography
description: Reflective framework for exploring the emotional and cultural roots of your money beliefs — scarcity thinking, family patterns, shame.

title: Rotating Savings Circles (ROSCAs) — How It Works
description: Tandas, susus, osusu — a centuries-old community wealth tool. Structure, practice, and how to start a rotating savings circle in your community.

title: Khan Academy Personal Finance
description: Free, self-paced personal finance covering budgeting, credit, saving, and insurance. Zero jargon.

title: Remember the Future — Art.coop
description: QTBIPOC creatives discuss building livelihoods rooted in care and cooperation — firing bosses, freeing land, and creating on their own terms. One of the best on-ramps for artists new to solidarity economics.

title: Remember the Future Fellowship
description: $15,000 plus technical assistance to arts/culture groups challenging dominant economic paradigms. Rolling applications.

title: NO STARVING ARTISTS! NO SELLOUTS! — Intro to Creative Work in the Solidarity Economy
description: A free course laying out principles and practices for building creative livelihoods outside the starve-or-sell-out binary. A practical on-ramp for cooperative economics.

title: Emergent Strategy — adrienne maree brown
description: Building adaptive, resilient movements using lessons from nature. Widely read in the community organizing and artist collective space.

title: Liberating Structures
description: Dozens of practical facilitation methods for building participation and collective intelligence in groups of any size.

title: Mutual Aid 101 — Dean Spade
description: What mutual aid is, how it differs from charity, how to build it. Essential for artist circles moving toward resource-sharing.

title: Mutual Aid Is Essential to Our Survival
description: The durable case for mutual aid as permanent infrastructure for communities that can't afford to wait for rescue.

title: The Conscious Citizens
description: A newsletter, directory, and global community dedicated to building collective consciousness and community power.

title: Conflict Resolution for Collectives
description: Practical toolkit for navigating conflict within artist groups — collective agreements, repair practices, facilitation guides. Open source and adaptable.

title: Peace Is Every Step + The Art of Power — Thich Nhat Hanh
description: Peace Is Every Step grounds mindfulness in daily life. The Art of Power reframes power as freedom, understanding, and love. Find both at your local library.

title: Zen and the Art of Saving the Planet — Online Course
description: A transformative online course bringing Thich Nhat Hanh's teachings to life. Balance personal wellbeing with climate action, master difficult emotions, train in deep listening, and turn climate concern into sustainable action. Join a community of changemakers.

title: Trying to Write in a Terrible World — Susan Muaddi Darraj
description: Darraj explores the Palestinian value of sumud — steadfast presence, refusing erasure — and what it means to write while bearing witness. An invitation to every artist navigating their practice in a world that gives many reasons to put down the pen.
